question.text: In a FLOATING-RATE bond, the bond's coupon resets periodically. The MAXIMUM duration (interest-rate sensitivity) at any point is approximately:

answer.text: The remaining time until the next coupon reset

explanation.text: The Logic: Floater duration ≈ time to next reset. Between resets, behaves like a short bond. After reset, coupon resets to market, returning to par. The Trap: Full maturity is wrong — that's the fixed-rate bond. Floater's short effective duration is its appeal for rate-rise environments. Cross-Exam Context: IV covers; XXI-B tests portfolio-manager choice. Manager's Pro-Tip: Floaters are ideal in rising-rate environments but don't provide price appreciation in falling-rate environments — know the trade-off.
